text:
maria: Quick triage note: after last week's transport refactor we're seeing host CPU increase ~10% on short interactive traffic (seq_len ~ 18). digging in.
cheng: symptom? kernel-level or syscall?
maria: perf collapsed to writev and tokenizer again. ran a flame and saw heavy hotpath in grpc assembly + writev fragmentation. Also noticed kernel selector picking a heavy throughput kernel for single-request batches.
alex: That matches my local repro. New http2 header packing yields many 64-256B iovecs; writev is called with dozens of small iovs which increases syscall cost and per-iovec overhead.
sam: And because we preparse upstream, KV keys were derived from tokenized form -> different keys when preparse toggles; that amplified eviction churn.
nora: Curious about selector logic. It uses average queue seq_len right? so a 1-request batch can inherit skewed stats.
cheng: Right. Selector heuristics: currently compute workload_profile = avg_seq_len(queue_window) and choose kernel based on that. For tiny bursts this misclassifies. Proposed changes:
- transport: coalesce adjacent small iovecs up to 4KB before writev (configurable max_coalesce_bytes)
- ingress: introduce `preparse_min_tokens` default 32, below which we skip preparse (avoid extra tokenization + cache churn)
- kernel selector: prefer per-batch feature (max_seq_len and candidate_batch_size) instead of global avg, and add override: if candidate_batch_size==1 and max_seq_len < 48 -> low-latency kernel
- kvcache: when preparse skipped, use stable request-hash (raw bytes) for keying instead of token-derived key (reduces churn)
maria: I prototyped a transport coalescer. microbench on short-chat workload (10k qps):
```
baseline: host_cpu 100%, p50 20ms, p99 290ms
+coalesce: host_cpu 91%, p50 21ms, p99 230ms
+coalesce + preparse_min_tokens=32: host_cpu 84%, p50 22ms, p99 170ms
+all + selector override: host_cpu 80%, p50 22ms, p99 150ms
```
(throughput steady)
alex: Nice. The p50 bump is expected due to skipping preparse, but p99/tail improved a lot. Worth it for interactive workloads.
sam: I kicked a canary at 1762254400 to canary-hosts-5, routing 9k short-rps. infra-bot please post metrics when ready.
infra-bot: Canary window 30m:
- host_cpu: -19.6%
- p50_lat: +0.8ms
- p99_lat: -48%
- kv_evictions/min: -36%
- transport.iov_coalesce_ratio: 0.82
- ingress.preparse_skipped_total: 17.2k

maria: Good signal. Next steps: land small patchset and gate by region. Low-risk rollout plan: Dedicated -> EU -> US Hosted.
cheng: PR plan: transport coalesce (#4210), ingress preparse gate (#4211), selector tuning (#4212), kvkey-stable (#4213). keep toggles default-on for canary but feature flags in runtime config.
nora: Tests we need: unit for coalescer correctness (ensure packet size limits respected), selector unit tests for singletons, integration test that verifies kvkey stability when preparse off.
alex: I'll own the transport PR. will include telemetry `transport.iov_coalesce_ratio` and an opt-out flag.
sam: I'll update dashboards: add `ingress.preparse_skipped_rate`, `selector.override_rate` and an alert if coalesce_ratio drops below 0.7. Also add nightly perf job for short-chat trace.
maria: Risk note: turning off preparse below threshold means one extra tokenize on GPU path for some requests; verify GPU kernel warmup unaffected. We'll monitor model-side tails.
cheng: Also add rollout check: no increase in large-request p50 > 5% during canary.
infra-bot: Canary promoted to staged (eu-west-1) at 1762254488 with 20% of short-traffic.
maria: Thanks team, PRs linked above. after staged 24h we can release in patch.
